## Résumé and professional experience

Name: Joseph Wilkes; also known as Joey Wilkes.
[Full résumé](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/resume/) | [Résumé PDF](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/resume/joseph-wilkes-resume.pdf) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joseph-b-wilkes) | [GitHub](https://github.com/JoeyWilkes12)

### Data Scientist & Data Science Consultant, Product Office — Anglepoint

Oct 2022 – Sept 2026 | Hybrid Remote from Utah, USA

- Launched Cloud Cost Management (FinOps) Services line of business to generate more than $100,000 USD through both client-facing delivery (3x) & product development
- Curated external product materials on FinOps & AI Cost Management services to support the 5th & 6th consecutive years as a Leader in the associated Gartner Magic Quadrant
- Innovated continuously to support a multi-year automation initiative to increase revenue per headcount for a major line of business, using LLMs to process thousands of text documents and automate consultants’ manual data collection & document extraction

### Data Engineer — Varian – A Siemens Healthineers Company

June 2022 – Oct 2022 | 100% Remote from Utah, USA

- Built a web-based Plotly Dash dashboard with 10+ data visualizations & 30+ interactive components to provide insights on an A/B test of clinicians’ use of AI models
- Engineered medical contouring data from nested & semi-structured to tabular form using Python with minimal guidance, providing statistics for an A/B test of AI performance
- Updated Airflow ETL DAGs involving 3+ sources & transferred 200+ GB of medical data from Azure to GCP BigQuery for AI & ML utilization
- Saved 12+ hours of contouring setup by automating a manual process using Python

### Analyst, SaaS Delivery — Anglepoint

May 2021 – June 2022 | On-site in Utah, USA

- Utilized Python, SQL, and Excel to identify millions of dollars in potential cost savings associated with management of Salesforce, Tableau, Adobe, & other SaaS vendors
- Received the Selflessness Company Core Value Award (Q3 2021)
- Built & led an internal Python resource group of 12+ individuals across several teams with a vision to enhance automation & analysis of client deliverables

### Research Assistant — Mathematics Department, B.Y.U.

Apr 2020 – May 2021 | Hybrid Remote from Utah, USA

- Engineered a data pipeline for a High Performance Computing (HPC) environment using Python, Slurm, Bash, and Git yielding 10+ TB of data through 40+ years of computing
- Automated processes for visualization & optimization of millions of predictive models
- Communicated & collaborated on technical concepts while writing a research paper, presenting at two research conferences, and teaching about HPC & code functionality

### Data Analytics Intern — Imagine Learning

May 2019 – Aug 2019 | On-site in Utah, USA

- Developed 12+ features for several predictive models using SQL & Python
- Acquired proficiency with Amazon Web Services (Athena, S3, Glue, Redshift, Lambda, EC2, IAM) as well as Google Cloud Platform, mainly Google Maps
- Engineered novel datasets for geospatial analysis & executive reporting

## Portfolio

- [How well can AI models play Queens?](https://joeywilkes12.github.io/queens-model-assessment/#/executive-summary): AI Evals. Extensive computational & scientific assessment of various AI models ability to play logical puzzle Queens. Tags: Frontier Foundation Models, Decision Models, Jev, OpenRouter, LangSmith, SubQ Snap. Also: [Open Queens Solver](https://joeywilkes12.github.io/queens-solver-router/).
- [FinOps FOCUS Explorer](https://joeywilkes12.github.io/finops-focus-router/): Cloud Cost Management. A cost dashboard, data explorer, and live use case queries over the FinOps FOCUS 1.0 sample billing data from Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Tags: Forecasting, time-series, Prophet, SQL, IT Financial Management, Cost Anomaly detection.
- [Agent Skills Resource Library](https://joeywilkes12.github.io/agent-skills-resource-library/): AI agents. Resources and guides for building, troubleshooting, and evaluating AI agent skills. Tags: MCP, Skills for AI agents, skill.md.
- [Queens Solver](https://joeywilkes12.github.io/queens-solver-router/): Turn a Queens screenshot into a solved board with computer vision and constraint solving. Technology: Python, OpenCV, Z3, Streamlit.
- Queens Solver example: a hard puzzle from 2026-10-04 solved in 20 seconds against a 4 minute 17 second player average (as of 5 October 2026, 03:20 UTC), with Python, OpenCV, Z3, Streamlit.

## Academic projects and research

### Reservoir Thinning

- [Learning Using Thinned Networks: A Crowdsourcing Phenomena in Reservoir Computing](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/reservoir-thinning/): Research on sparse reservoir networks that reconstruct the Lorenz attractor, connecting network thinning, spectral radius, and response diversity.
- Authors: J. Jamieson, D. J. Passey, B. Webb, J. Wilkes. Document date: April 15, 2022.
- Topics: Reservoir computing, Network science, Chaotic systems.
- [Original report PDF (15 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/reservoir-thinning.pdf)

### RISK Game Prediction

- [RISK Data Project Fall 2020](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/risk-game-prediction/): Game simulation, feature engineering, and machine learning to predict the winner of RISK from the current board state.
- Authors: Jacob Murri, Joseph Wilkes, Caleb Wilson, Lukas Erekson. Document date: December 10, 2020.
- Topics: Machine learning, Simulation, Data engineering.
- [Original report PDF (17 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/risk-game-prediction.pdf)

### General Conference NLP

- [A Natural Language Processing Analysis of General Conference Discourses Employing Time-Series and Classification Models](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/general-conference-nlp/): Topic modeling, speaker classification, and related-talk retrieval using NLP and time-series methods on General Conference discourses.
- Authors: Clark Brown, Mikelle Rogers, Daniel Swingle, Joseph Wilkes, Caleb Wilson. Document date: April 15, 2021.
- Topics: Natural language processing, Time series, Recommendation systems.
- [Original report PDF (17 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/general-conference-nlp.pdf)

### Predicting Movie Revenue

- [Let's All Go To The Movies](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/prediction-movie-revenue/): A comparison of random forests, nearest neighbors, and neural networks for predicting domestic and worldwide movie revenue.
- Authors: Joseph Wilkes, Jacob Rohde, Pauline Caussé. Document date: Fall 2019.
- Topics: Machine learning, Regression, Feature engineering.
- [Original report PDF (6 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/prediction-movie-revenue.pdf)

### Non-Trivial Evasion

- [Non-Trivial Evasion](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/non-trivial-evasion/): Optimal control models for fox-and-rabbit evasion using linear-quadratic regulation and Pontryagin's maximum principle.
- Authors: Taylor Gledhill, Joseph Wilkes, Raelynn Wonnacott, Nathan Nelson. Document date: April 2021.
- Topics: Optimal control, Dynamical systems, Mathematical modeling.
- [Original report PDF (10 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/non-trivial-evasion.pdf)

### Non-Trivial Pursuit

- [Non-Trivial Pursuit](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/non-trivial-pursuit/): Mathematical models of pursuit and evasion, testing how destination, terrain, prediction, and escape strategies shape a chase.
- Authors: Taylor Gledhill, Joseph Wilkes, Raelynn Wonnacott, Nathan Nelson. Document date: December 2020.
- Topics: Dynamical systems, Numerical modeling, Pursuit and evasion.
- [Original report PDF (10 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/non-trivial-pursuit.pdf)

### Childhood Computational Thinking

- [Evaluation of Childhood Computational Thinking with ScratchJR and Robot Toys: A Literature Review](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/academic-experience/literature-review/): A literature review comparing ScratchJr and educational robots as tools for developing computational thinking in young children.
- Authors: Joseph Wilkes.
- Topics: Computational thinking, Education, Literature review.
- [Original report PDF (16 pages)](https://joey-wilkes-home.vercel.app/assets/reports/literature-review.pdf)

### Applied Mathematics Projects

- [Applied Mathematics Projects](https://github.com/JoeyWilkes12/Projects1): Python implementations of graph algorithms, numerical methods, Markov chains, nearest neighbors, Monte Carlo integration, and unit testing.
- Topics: Python, Graph algorithms, Numerical methods, Markov chains, Unit testing.
- Implementations: Breadth-first search, Binary trees, Conditioning and stability, Differentiation, Drazin inverse, K-nearest neighbors, Markov chains, Monte Carlo integration, Newton's method, PageRank, Unit testing, Wordle solver.
